breakdown.summary: A 44 s motion-graphics ad for an AI assistant app (HowDo), posted by a studio (sleeko) as a showreel: the ad plays inside a constant presentation frame (purple gradient, studio logo, a rounded inner frame of ~75 % width, four chapter buttons Intro / Problem / Use Case / Call to Action whose fill moves as the progress, a tick ruler). Inside, a voice-over is illustrated line by line: white cards with kinetic typography (typed word by word, words swapped for icon rows, letters sliding), 3D phone and monitor mockups with screen clips, four short live-action plates, and instant scene switches instead of transitions. A third of all frames are holds: the animation moves, then rests on a card or a pose for 0.2-1.0 s, then moves again. Measured 1440x1080 at 30 fps CFR, 1332 frames, 111.7 BPM; the lab's '4.1 cuts/min' is wrong for the inner picture - the presentation frame hid about 14 instant switches from the cut detector (reviewed as hard_cut events).

The voice-over starts at f73 (00:00:02:13) 'Every day, there's something you've never done before'. What stops the scroll: a real hand + phone (familiar), a brand name rising out of it, playful 3D objects, and the showreel frame with chapter buttons that promises a structured case study.

The live plates show no real camera move; the whole-frame numbers are diluted by the static presentation frame (~75 % of the width is the picture).
breakdown.grade: Measured (colour.py): cool, magenta tint, bright (high-key), high contrast, 'crushed blacks' and 'vignette' - but the blacks and the vignette are the presentation frame's dark edges and purple gradient, not a grade on the ad. The ad itself is high-key: white / lilac (#f7e8f7, #db9cf8) cards with deep-purple (#5d3f7b) type, soft warm-grey live plates, pastel backgrounds behind the mockups; consistent for the whole length (brightness spread 7 %). The outro clouds are the only saturated, low-key picture (f1303-1331).
breakdown.rhythm: Move - rest - move: 34 % of all frames are exact holds, typically 0.2-1.0 s (E014 17 f, E030 18 f, E033 30 f, E019 64 f), each rest sitting on a finished word, logo or pose, then the next line of the voice-over triggers the next move. About 14 scene switches in 44 s (~19/min, not the lab's 4.1 cuts/min). Not cut to the beat: only E022 f612 lands on a beat and E041's last letter on the drop f1212; the pizza hold starts on the drop f762. Words land 1-2 frames apart (E028: one word every 2 frames), holds end a few frames before the next spoken line.
rebuild_tips: Write the voice-over first and time everything to it: one white card per spoken line, the words typed in 1-2 frames apart (Fusion Text+ with Write On, or HyperFrames per-word reveals), then HOLD the finished line 0.3-1.0 s until the next line starts.

Switch scenes with instant cuts that land in motion (the new card's words already sliding / typing on the first frame), and use blur-outs only at chapter changes (a 15-frame blur + white-out, S-curve).
Replace words with icon rows for 'something / new / exciting' lines (E004-E006): the word lifts out, 3-4 outline icons cycle in its place, 5-10 frames per swap.
Put your product in 3D mockups (phone, monitor) with a screen clip inside, and push a live plate in beside it (a 29-frame push, S-curve) instead of cutting to it.
End on the drop: typewriter the last line so the final letter lands on the beat drop, cut to a calm plate (clouds), pop the mark in and type the wordmark, fade the picture to black over ~1 s.

The showreel frame (chapter buttons with a moving progress fill) is a presentation layer for posting the case study - build it as a HyperFrames graphic with four pills and a sliding fill, and keep the ad itself at the inner size.
